summary: Ichisada Miyazaki (1901–1995) was a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1922–1925) under Jitsuzo Kuwabara and later held a post at Kyoto University from circa 1936 to 1965.
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied at the Sapienza University of Rome, where he later served as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University (~1936–1941), he held posts at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, Pravda, and the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Ihsan Ali (born 1955) works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peshawar and under Frank Raymond Allchin, later serving as Director of Archaeology and Museums in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Vice Chancellor of Hazara University.

Ikko Arai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from Komazawa University. Arai studied under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.

Ikuhisa Takigawa (born 1968) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Waseda University, he served as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Waseda University and Tokai University, attested in 2002.

Ikuko Tazaki is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. In 2017, she was attested as a special researcher at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute and an affiliate researcher at Kyoto University.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen (born 1959) is a religious studies scholar and philosopher. He earned his PhD at the University of Helsinki studying under René Gothóni, later working there as an Academy Research Fellow and as a visiting researcher at Oxford.

Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) was a philosopher who studied at Collegium Fridericianum and the University of Königsberg (1740–1746). In 1770, he assumed the chair of logic and metaphysics at the University of Königsberg.

Imre Galambos (born 1967) is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at ELTE, Nankai, and UC Berkeley, and held posts at the British Library, Cambridge, and Zhejiang University.

Imre Hamar (born 1967) specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki, later becoming a professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006.

In-gun Kang specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Kang studied at the Jesuit School of Theology, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Heythrop College, University of London, under supervisors including Michael Barnes and Aloysius Pieris.

Ines Konczak-Nagel specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She has held posts as a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University in 2012 and as a postdoctoral research fellow at the Berlin State Museums.
Ingmar Heise works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University by 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.
Ingo Strauch is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He received his PhD from the Free University of Berlin by 2000 and served as a professor at the University of Lausanne, attested in 2018.
Inyoung Chung is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner, attested in 2008.

Ioan Petru Culianu (1950–1991) was a scholar of religion and history. He studied at Bucharest, Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, and Sorbonne, working with Mircea Eliade, and held posts at Groningen and the University of Chicago Divinity School.

Irawati Karve (1905–1970) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Huzurpaga, Fergusson College, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye, later holding a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1959–1960).

Irfan Habib (born 1931) is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (~1947–1953), and New College, Oxford (~1954–1958), and began serving as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University circa 1953.

Irving Babbitt (1865–1933) was a philosopher who studied at Williams College, Harvard, and the University of Paris. He held academic posts at Williams College (~1893–1894) and Harvard University (~1894–1933).
